observation: Builder src/render/opticCellPresentation.js. Spent reuses the same cached octahedral shard as diamond (opticCellGeometry 111-126, key 'optic:prism') and swaps only the shared material: cached 'optic:body:spent' MeshPhysicalMaterial (lines 212-242) — opaque-ish smoky alpha (opacity 0.88), no iridescence, near-dead emissive. Its 5 internal inclusions use the cached 'optic:facet:dead' material (279-289, 295) and are re-skinned at runtime, not rebuilt: syncOpticCellSkin compares the stamped kind and calls applyOpticCellSkin (438-451), which reuses the existing detail meshes (357-368). Spend/rekindle is a reference swap, never a new geometry or program (module header 21-27; test/optic-materials.test.mjs:148-181 flips live->spent->live through the asteroid motion seam). Distinct dead-prism role is deliberate versus live diamond (header 17-20; test lines 110-122 measure darker color, thicker alpha, no iridescence). No per-cell material allocation; the prism body geometry is shared with diamond and only differs by material reference.
decision: No construction change recommended; the dead state is a shared-material swap on the same mesh, which is the intended cheap runtime path. Recommend needs follow-up because no current visual evidence shows the dead state at gameplay scale.
next: Needs a current capture of a discharged cell beside a live diamond (ceres prism gallery or swarm arena spend/rekindle) plus draw cost; visual evidence is the acceptance path.
